correctness.rationale: The two block sets have 26 distinct triples and exactly one block through each of 78 unordered point pairs. If three cross-free classes each had size four, 20 blocks avoiding the sole unused point would require distinct same-class pairs, but only 18 exist; explicit size-three examples attain the bound. Two independent exhaustive programs test all 200200 candidate unordered triples in each of the two 13-point systems, construct and symmetrically verify all legal exchanges, and compute components and their degree patterns. Their exact state/edge/component numbers agree. A general all-or-none insertion lemma proves degrees must be multiples of three; the seven-state components additionally have a unique six-degree center and two triangles on the leaves.

value.rationale: This is the first order with two nonisomorphic Steiner triple systems, a natural complete comparison universe. Cross-free classes are motivated by Gyárfás 2015 extremal questions. The exact placement census (6214 versus 6148) and complete one-point-exchange component classification measure sensitivity of an extremal avoidance configuration to a Pasch switch: 39 K4 plus 156 isolates versus 18 K4, four glued-K4 seven-state motifs and 144 isolates. The general exchange lemma gives structural explanation. No downstream general theorem or asymptotic application is asserted.
